narrative.summary: WHO has issued global guidance on the ethics and governance of AI in health (2021), extended in 2024–2025 to large multi-modal (generative) models, and a set of regulatory considerations for AI in health (2023). It has also published a framework for generating evidence on AI-based medical devices. The World Health Assembly has not adopted a resolution dedicated to AI; AI governance was discussed in 2026 under an agenda item on data, digital health and AI. WHO regional committees have adopted AI resolutions: the Pan American Health Organization's Directing Council approved a policy on data science in public health using AI in 2021, and the Regional Committee for the Western Pacific endorsed regional guidance on responsible AI in health in 2026. PAHO also published the AI-GUARD tool for assessing AI initiatives in health (2026).
lead_institutions: WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific

instruments.official_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
instruments.english_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
instruments.summary: WHO guidance on artificial intelligence in health. It sets out six consensus principles (protect autonomy; promote well-being, safety and the public interest; ensure transparency, explainability and intelligibility; foster responsibility and accountability; ensure inclusiveness and equity; promote responsive and sustainable AI) and recommendations for governments, developers and providers on governance, liability, data protection and oversight of AI used in health.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization on 28 June 2021.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 28 June 2021 printed on WHO publication page (ISBN 9789240029200). Executive summary is a separate item (9789240037403), not recorded separately. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 28 June 2021 and 'six consensus principles' confirmed.; 'Non-binding' and 'first global guidance' not stated on the page.

instruments.official_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
instruments.english_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
instruments.summary: Guidance applying WHO's AI ethics principles to large multi-modal models (generative AI) in health. It describes uses in diagnosis, patient-guided use, clerical tasks, education and research, sets out risks, and gives over 40 recommendations for governments, developers and providers across the design, development and deployment of such models, including regulation, audits, impact assessments and liability.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization; the publication page is dated 25 March 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: WHO publication page (ISBN 9789240084759) prints 25 March 2025. The guidance was first released on 18 January 2024 (per WHO news release, not re-verified); the page now carries the 2025 version only, so the printed 2025 date is used. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title and 25 March 2025 date confirmed on the WHO page; recommendation count and audiences not on the landing page (taken as from the PDF).; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health
instruments.english_title: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health
instruments.summary: Sets out key regulatory considerations for AI systems in health for regulators, developers and manufacturers, grouped under documentation and transparency, risk management and life-cycle approach, intended use and analytical and clinical validation, data quality, privacy and data protection, and engagement and collaboration among regulators, patients, providers and industry.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization on 19 October 2023 as a high-level overview of considerations; WHO states it is not intended as guidance, as a regulatory framework or policy.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 19 October 2023 printed on WHO publication page. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 19 Oct 2023 and audiences confirmed. Page states the overview is 'not intended as guidance, as a regulatory framework or policy'.

instruments.official_title: Generating Evidence for Artificial Intelligence Based Medical Devices: A Framework for Training Validation and Evaluation
instruments.english_title: Generating evidence for artificial intelligence-based medical devices: a framework for training, validation and evaluation
instruments.summary: Framework for developers, regulators and health authorities on generating clinical and technical evidence for AI-based medical devices across their life cycle, covering data management, model training, validation and evaluation, and post-market monitoring.

instruments.official_title: CD59.R2 - Policy on the Application of Data Science in Public Health Using Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies
instruments.english_title: Resolution CD59.R2: Policy on the Application of Data Science in Public Health Using Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies
instruments.issuing_authority: Pan American Health Organization, 59th Directing Council / 73rd Session of the Regional Committee of WHO for the Americas
instruments.publisher_name: Pan American Health Organization, 59th Directing Council / 73rd Session of the Regional Committee of WHO for the Americas
instruments.summary: Resolution of the WHO Regional Committee for the Americas adopting a regional policy (document CD59/7) on data science in public health using AI and other emerging technologies, built on principles including people-centredness, ethical and human-rights grounding, transparency, data protection, open and shareable algorithms and data, and non-discriminatory, human-controlled technology. It urges Member States to build capacity for AI-supported health analysis, address data bias, and develop national and subnational policies and legal frameworks based on the regional policy, and asks the PAHO Director to support a regional roadmap and report periodically.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the 59th Directing Council of PAHO (73rd Session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Americas) at its second meeting on 20 September 2021. The policy it approves (document CD59/7, 12 July 2021) provides for an evaluation in 2026.

instruments.official_title: AI-GUARD Tool: Artificial Intelligence Governance & Use Assessment for Responsible Deployment
instruments.english_title: AI-GUARD Tool: Artificial Intelligence Governance & Use Assessment for Responsible Deployment
instruments.issuing_authority: Pan American Health Organization (PAHO/WHO), with the Inter-American Development Bank
instruments.publisher_name: Pan American Health Organization (PAHO/WHO), with the Inter-American Development Bank
instruments.summary: Tiered pre-implementation assessment framework for AI initiatives in health, organised around four pillars (governance and accountability, risk and bias safeguards, use and human control, deployment readiness) and three tiers, from responsible AI use through program-level AI to high-impact AI governance. Assessments result in one of three decisions (proceed, temporary conditional authorization pending verification, or reconsider/redesign), and annexes set vendor evidence and model-card requirements and an incident response and emergency deactivation protocol. It is aimed at ministries of health, public health agencies, hospitals, national health programs and regulatory and oversight bodies.
instruments.current_status: Published by PAHO with the Inter-American Development Bank; PAHO document page dated 18 June 2026, title page 'Washington, D.C., 2026'. Described as a structured advisory instrument that does not replace national regulatory frameworks, legal review processes or procurement rules. Spanish version also published.

instruments.english_title: Regional Committee for the Western Pacific resolution WPR/RC77.R1 on artificial intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific (77th session)
instruments.publisher_name: WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific (77th session)
instruments.summary: Resolution of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific endorsing the draft 'Guidance for Responsible AI in Health in the Western Pacific Region'. It urges Member States, considering their contexts and capacities, to apply the guidance to the design, implementation, evaluation and governance of AI in health, to strengthen cross-government coordination, and to build AI capacity among policy-makers, implementers, clinicians and the public. It asks the Regional Director to provide technical support on AI governance, facilitate knowledge sharing among countries and areas, and report periodically on AI governance and implementation for health in the Region.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the fifth meeting of the 77th session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific on 21 October 2026. It endorses the regional guidance in draft form; a Chinese version of the resolution is also published.
